_comment: Section 57 and the Search Console numbers behind it. 339 of 526 indexable
pages carried a <title> longer than Google prints, and 9,273 characters of
that were boilerplate: 245 pages ended '| MODUNERA Tiny House' (22 characters)
The obvious move — strip the words 'Tiny House' from every suffix — is wrong,
and measuring said so. Of the 245, only 97 already carry the phrase before the
pipe. On the other 148 the suffix is the only place the keyword appears, and
removing it would trade a truncation problem for a relevance one.
So the rule is conditional: the suffix is shortened only where the title has
already said it. The remaining pages keep their keyword and are shortened at
the source instead, in the generator that composes them.
og:title carries the same string as <title> on this site, so both are rewritten
together. The JSON-LD headline is the body without the suffix and is untouched.
keyword_note: Matched case-insensitively against the title body, before the final pipe. Written as a pattern so 'Tiny-House-Siedlung' counts.

suffix_rules.note: All 108 of these already name the subject in the body; 'Ratgeber' is a section label, not a search term anyone types.

target_note: Google truncates on pixel width, not characters, so 60 is an approximation. tools/score-titles.mjs also reports an em width so a short title of wide capitals is not passed by a count that happens to fit.
